column1: # One line per task, tab-separated: cr<TAB>wave<TAB>task<TAB>state<TAB>what it is
# The PO asked "how many waves and tasks are there and how many completed" and the
# answer could not be produced. The BUGS half was one command, because defects live
# in a CSV with a status column. The waves half was impossible, because tasks are
# written as sentences scattered through 30,000-70,000 characters per change
# request. Three extraction attempts gave three different answers and the first was
# silently wrong: an unscoped search matched ONE change request's "6 waves, 34
# tasks" against all nine and printed it nine times as though each had been
# measured. It looked like a clean table.
# So the STATE moves here where a script can read it. The narrative stays in
# 11-change-requests.md, which is what it is good at.
# STATES, and a script refuses any other (the G46 lesson - a column holding two
# vocabularies makes every count taken from it wrong):
#   done     the task is built and proved
#   verify   built, not yet proved - it is not done
#   open     not started, or started and not finished
#   blocked  cannot proceed; the reason belongs in the change request
# ⚠ PO STEER 2026-08-28: "I will not worry too much on 2 - Make task progress
# countable." NOBODY BACK-FILLS THIS AND IT DOES NOT BECOME A GATE. Rows accumulate
# only where a lane owning a wave finds them useful. Do not spend a lane on coverage.
# ⚠ SEEDED WITH SIX ROWS, NOT BACK-FILLED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
# These six are the only tasks anywhere in the register already written in a
# countable shape (CR-046 wave A). The other eight change requests record their
# tasks as prose, and back-filling them would mean extracting truth from sentences
# - the exact thing that produced the wrong table above. A lane that OWNS a wave
# adds its rows here when it starts. `10-scripts/wave_report.py` names every change
# request with nothing recorded, so the gap is counted rather than silent.
